absent: Exact device, system device, processor and interrupt primitives invoked during image creation are outside these fragments.
Full layout of task, page, zone, bitmap and platform operation structures beyond fields touched here.
Timeout value, wakeup detection internals, workqueue freeze mechanics and refrigerator entry behavior.
Image size, reserved size, speed calculation constants and page flag definitions.

findings.text: Two global routines manage allocation constraints around power transitions, one tightening allowed operations and one restoring prior allowance, with nesting support so repeated tightening needs matching restores.

Global routines coordinate freezing of kernel threads and later restart, using a shared internal helper that repeatedly attempts to freeze tasks until none remain, timeout expires, or a wakeup is pending.

Global routines preallocate memory for a hibernate image, release snapshot resources and reset accounting, clear reclaimed free pages after restore, record free pages in a map, and report elapsed transfer performance.
A weak default resume helper reports success and may be overridden by architecture code to perform post restore actions when not remaining in the suspended state.

Image creation moves through device suspension, platform pre snapshot check, secondary processor shutdown, interrupt suppression and system device suspension, low level state save and architectural suspension with matching restore and tracing, then unwinds in reverse order through system device resume, interrupt enable, processor enable, platform finish and device resume with mode dependent message selection, aborting early on failures or test and wakeup conditions.

Task freezing announces its target and optionally prepares workqueues, then loops scanning all threads except the caller, counting remaining freezable tasks plus workqueue busy state, exiting when empty, on timeout, or on pending wakeup, sleeping with growing delay between passes, and finally reporting success or detailed failure with diagnostics.
Platform specific pre snapshot, leave and finish actions run only when platform mode is requested and platform operations are present, otherwise they are no operations returning success.
Disabling secondary processors is paired with idle handling pause before and resume after, and enabling reverses the order, keeping idle management symmetric around processor transitions.

Restriction saves the current allowance once and removes input output and filesystem related permissions, further nested calls only bump a counter, while restore decrements and only reinstates the saved allowance when the last holder exits.

A position reset points the cursor at the first zone and leaf with cleared offsets and sentinel current value, forward iteration scans set positions within the current block then advances across leaves and zones until exhaustion, signalling end with a dedicated sentinel, and clearing affects the most recently returned position.

Bitmap creation initializes a chained allocator and empty zone list, builds extents then per zone structures sized to cover each range, resets position on success and frees everything on failure, while lookup reuses the cached zone and node when the target falls inside them and otherwise searches zones and descends levels to locate leaf storage and update the cached position.

Image page allocation obtains cleared pages and marks them in forbidden and free maps, retrying while a safe request yields a page already recorded free, counting such unsafe encounters, and safe allocation first reuses a dedicated list with explicit clearing before falling back to the general path.

Restore protection exists in two compile variants, one tracking an active flag that gates making a restored page writable and cleared at the end, the other providing empty operations that always report success.

Release walks free and forbidden maps in lockstep to free only pages present in both, clears their marks, restores protections and resets image accounting and list pointers, while preallocation creates three tracking maps, estimates saveable and free capacity across zones, derives limits from reserves and desired image size, applies memory pressure if oversubscribed, allocates from high and normal pools, drops surplus pages, measures duration, and releases everything on allocation failure.

Post restore free page handling only scans when poisoning or initialization on free is enabled, validates each frame before clearing, resets iteration afterwards, and always touches the watchdog while advancing across blocks.
Allocation mask restriction and restoration require the system transition mutex to be held by the caller, otherwise a warning is emitted.
Freezing scans and thawing scans hold the task list in read mode while iterating all process threads, releasing before sleeping or reporting and reacquiring for diagnostics.

Snapshot tracking uses a bitmap object holding a zone list, allocation chain and cursor with current zone, node, node offset, current frame and bit index, where each zone records start and end frames, tree depth, block count, root pointer and node and leaf lists, supporting blockwise iteration and radix descent.

Small object allocation for bitmap construction uses a chain object holding head link, used offset, allocation mask and safety requirement, carving successive requests from linked data pages and acquiring a fresh cleared page when remaining space is insufficient.

Freezing can fail with busy status when tasks refuse to freeze or work remains busy after timeout or wakeup, triggering diagnostic dumps and thaw of kernel threads on the kernel only path, while image creation aborts with logged errors when device or system device suspension fails and reports creation errors without aborting the resume unwind.

Missing free map during post restore clearing, lookup of a frame outside all zones, and failed zone or block allocation are treated as serious faults with warnings or fatal checks, and image preallocation failures release partial state and return out of memory.
